record.title: Anthropic releases Haiku 5.5 with reported computer-use gains and lower per-token prices
record.summary: Anthropic announced Claude Haiku 5.5 on 7 October 2026 (model ID claude-haiku-5-5) and says it is available on its platform and major cloud providers. The release reports 72.4% on the OSWorld 2.1 offline subset and publishes API prices by prompt length. Its system-card executive summary additionally reports no new Responsible Scaling Policy thresholds, low assessed misalignment risk under its evaluations, tested prompt-injection robustness, and an over-refusal caveat. These are provider-reported findings; the card summary was inspected, but detailed protocols and independent matched results remain unavailable.

claims.label: DEMONSTRATED
claims.text: Anthropic announced Claude Haiku 5.5 on 2026-10-07 with model ID claude-haiku-5-5 and made it available through its Claude Platform and major cloud platforms.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: Anthropic reports Haiku 5.5 scored 72.4% on the offline subset of OSWorld 2.1, versus 15.7% for Haiku 4.5 and 48.9% for GPT-6 Luna in its published comparison; these are provider-reported evaluations, not independent results.

claims.label: DEMONSTRATED
claims.text: Anthropic’s published API price table lists Haiku 5.5 at $0.10 input / $0.50 output per million tokens for prompts up to 100,000 tokens, and $0.50 input / $2.50 output above 100,000 tokens.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: Anthropic’s system-card summary reports that Haiku 5.5 crossed no new Responsible Scaling Policy thresholds, had low assessed misalignment risk under the evaluations described, showed stronger cyber capability than Haiku 4.5 but below larger models, and was robust to tested prompt injections; it also reports the highest over-refusal rate among models in its automated behavioral audit.

evidence_gaps.description: Performance and safety comparisons are provider-reported. The system-card executive summary is now accessible and inspected, but full protocols, sample sizes and detailed results were not reviewed; no independent matched evaluation or cost-per-completed-task analysis was conducted.

brief.importance_rationale: If the reported performance and pricing hold under matched independent evaluations, a small model with stronger computer-use results and much lower token prices could expand high-volume agent workloads and change the cost/performance boundary. Current benchmark comparisons and savings are Anthropic-reported and not independently verified.
limitations: The benchmark table and customer examples are published by Anthropic; no independent reproduction or direct customer data audit was performed.
List-price discounts do not establish lower cost per completed task; the release notes an updated tokenizer that can use slightly more tokens per task.
Benchmark figures are limited to the stated versions and settings; the OSWorld result is for the offline subset, and wider production performance is unmeasured here.

The system-card executive summary was inspected, but detailed evaluation sections, protocols, sample sizes and underlying results were not; all reported comparisons remain provider-authored and unverified independently.

technical.claimed_result: Anthropic reports 72.4% on the OSWorld 2.1 offline subset for Haiku 5.5, versus 15.7% for Haiku 4.5 and 48.9% for GPT-6 Luna; these comparisons have not been independently reproduced.

brief.title: Anthropic releases Haiku 5.5 with reported computer-use gains and lower per-token prices
brief.why_it_matters: A smaller model with reported gains on computer-use and other agent benchmarks at much lower token prices could expand high-volume agent workloads. Whether it improves cost per completed task depends on matched performance, effort, latency, token use and tool settings; independent comparisons are still needed.
